article_title: Non-native insects dominate daytime pollination in a high-elevation Hawaiian dryland ecosystem
version_package_role: byte-transport fallback when legacy per-file stream endpoints fail; provenance is locked on extracted source files rather than the dynamically assembled ZIP container
raw_data_scope: The recovered Dryad package contains raw flower-visitation observations and keys. It does not contain a source-native manual-flower-treatment table. The published bagging result is therefore retained as article-level context only and is not reconstructed as raw species-level treatment values.
claim_boundary: This is one Hawaii Island dryland ecosystem containing eight focal native plants. Visitation identity/frequency and manual flower-treatment outcomes must remain distinct. Species within this study are plant-level response panels, not eight independent systems. Non-native visitor dominance does not by itself establish equivalent pollination service, and the published seed-set dependence does not identify historical floral evolution.
